removed.text: He wears a tall felt hat.
removed.reason: Machal p.240 describes his hair, eyes, coat of hair, cloak, belt and red shirt but says nothing of a hat; find for "felt hat" across the corpus returns 0 hits.

downgraded.text: When a newly bought animal is first brought home, in several places its owner bows to the four corners of the stall and says, "Here is a shaggy beast for thee, Master! Love him, give him to eat and to drink!", then ties its lead to the kitchen-stove.
downgraded.to_text: When a newly bought animal is first brought home, in several places its owner bows to each of the four corners of the building and says, "Here is a shaggy beast for thee, Master! Love him, give him to eat and to drink!", then ties its lead to the kitchen-stove.
downgraded.reason: Ralston p.126 says the owner turns to each of the four corners of the building, not of the stall; wording narrowed to the page.

flagged.reason: Ralston pp.122-123 names the place Lusatia, not a people; Sorbs is the people that place is taken to fix, which the page itself does not print. The same applies to the peoples value of /variants/1.

flagged.text: He is everywhere given to grumbling and quarrelling, in strong, idiomatic phrases.
flagged.reason: Ralston p.122 says this holds "every where", not specifically in the Viatka district; the text is supported but its placement under the Viatka variant may read as regional.

flagged.text: In other places his appearance is much the same, but sometimes he wears a blue caftan with a rose-coloured girdle.
flagged.reason: Ralston p.122 gives this for "other places", not the Viatka district; supported, but placed under the Viatka variant.

grade_rationale.text: Machal records the Domovoy among the Russians, and records the White Russians' homage to him and the Little Russians' Didko or Domovyk as the same genius.
Ralston records Domovoy beliefs among the Russians and the Ruthenians, in Lusatia and in Poland.
Afanasyev records the domovoi in the Great Russian provinces and under the name padpechka among the Belarusians.
Ralston cites Afanasief for the January offering, so Ralston and Afanasyev are counted as one source; Machal is counted separately, giving at least two independent sources for several peoples.
